8f3989339145fde6a96e3e9e40864516ecae181f.summary: Blog post by Matt Graeber, published 2017-12-22, describing code signing attacks in which an attacker clones a legitimate Microsoft certificate chain and trusts the cloned root on victim systems, so malicious code appears Microsoft-signed. It explains why signature validation accepts such chains, how root CA installation can be detected with Sysmon, how per-user root trust can be restricted through a registry setting, and how root trust can be checked against the authroot.stl list. It also names the Microsoft flight root as a possible cloning candidate.

8f02e50e937228476c2898f3f02dd74fd6a43340.summary: Annual roundup by Patrick Wardle (Objective-See) of new macOS malware first seen in 2022, with analysis and sample downloads. It covers about a dozen families, including SysJoker, DazzleSpy, CoinMiner, CloudMensis, rShell and Insekt, plus adware and older threats in an appendix. Several spread by typosquatting or supply-chain compromise, others via trojanized disk images or browser exploits, and infection vectors are unknown for several. Findings are credited to vendor researchers including TrendMicro, ESET, Intezer, Talos, SentinelOne, Volexity, Sonatype and ReversingLabs.
